audits.title: AI crawler vs conversational agent separation
audits.purpose: Not all AI bots are the same. Training crawlers like GPTBot, CCBot, and Google-Extended scrape your content to build datasets, while conversational and retrieval agents like ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, and OAI-SearchBot fetch pages live to answer real user questions and can send referral traffic back to you. Many sites want to block the former while welcoming the latter — but a single catch-all User-agent: * cannot express that distinction. Granular robots.txt governance names both categories explicitly so each gets the access policy you actually intend.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Named training/realtime robots groups and root allowance. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Absent policy and unnamed permissive catch-all NA. Named coverage across categories or differing category allowance can pass; other named cases warn; unnamed blanket block fails.
review.proposedWork: Describe policy control, not a mandatory number of bot groups. Equivalent effective policies should not change quality merely because one spells out extra names. Keep intentional restrictions explicit.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Equivalent wildcard/named policies, intentional broad deny, category-specific rules, duplicate groups and deep Allow exceptions.

audits.title: Documented AI bots allowed by robots.txt
audits.purpose: Reports your robots.txt stance on five long-tail AI bot tokens in one place. Only the bots whose operator publishes crawler documentation — YouBot (You.com) and AI2Bot (Allen Institute) — affect the score, because only those directives have a documented reader. Bytespider, cohere-ai and Diffbot are listed for information: blocking them is a legitimate operational choice that costs no AI-answer visibility.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Root robots rules for five long-tail tokens. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Absent/unparseable policy NA. YouBot and AI2Bot root blocks decide failure; Bytespider, cohere-ai and Diffbot remain advisory. Named or inherited allowance passes.
review.proposedWork: Keep supported consumers separate from the advisory population. Root policy is independent of page purpose and does not prove deep-path access.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Each scored/advisory token alone, wildcard inheritance, named exceptions and root/deep-path disagreement.

audits.title: AI usage-preference declaration
audits.purpose: Where a site declares how AI systems may use its content. The IETF AIPREF work attaches that preference to a Content-Usage response header or a robots.txt rule, and explicitly leaves the HTML head out of scope; the head-level noai/noimageai convention has real adoption but no AI vendor documents honoring it. This audit reports what a site declares and where, and never treats declaring nothing as a defect.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Origin Content-Usage and page headers/meta conventions. Grade D; experimental tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Any AIPREF declaration passes ahead of opt-out-convention warnings; no declaration NA.
review.proposedWork: Optional declaration presence only. Preserve each channel/resource and avoid implying syntax validity or consumer enforcement. Keep grade D experimental status; validity belongs to its separate audit.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Absent convention, malformed adopted declaration, different pages/channels, opt-out beside a preference and stable provenance.

audits.title: AI crawlers get the same response from the edge that browsers get
audits.purpose: Fetches the homepage, sampled content URLs and /llms.txt once as a browser and once per published AI crawler User-Agent, then classifies every difference: Cloudflare challenge, pay-per-crawl 402, proof-of-work wall, rate limit, opaque 403, or a 200 carrying a fraction of the text. Reports per crawler and per URL, and scores a block only where robots.txt said the crawler was welcome.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Shared UA probes of root, bounded sitemap URLs and llms.txt when served. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No probes or no successful baseline NA. Robots-consistent blocks become notes; hard deltas fail; ambiguous deltas warn; otherwise pass.
review.proposedWork: Per-URL probe comparisons independent of page type. Exclude unusable baselines per pair, not only when all baselines fail. Impersonated UA results do not establish verified crawler behavior. Expose sample and unknown policy.
review.acceptanceCriteria: One failed baseline among good pairs, deliberate path block, unknown robots, mounted URL, missing probes and limited sitemap coverage.

review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No declarations NA; cross-channel opposite values over overlapping scopes fail. Page declarations can default to `/`; same-channel pairs are skipped.
review.proposedWork: Preserve resource scope before comparison. Different page policies must not become origin-wide contradictions. Fetch permission and usage permission need distinct meanings. Line order alone cannot identify CDN ownership.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Opposite policies on disjoint pages, same-page conflict, agent-specific rules, path boundaries, same-channel contradictions and partial reads.

review.acceptanceCriteria: Free pages plus paid page, page-scoped RSL, unread external license, malformed price/challenge, duplicate baseline observations and cache directives.

review.acceptanceCriteria: Named/wildcard precedence, absent policy, root allowed with deep URL blocked and the reverse; unchanged outcome across page labels. Add token-specific legacy/control cases where relevant.

audits.title: PerplexityBot allowed
audits.purpose: Reads the robots.txt rules that apply to PerplexityBot — its own group if it has one, otherwise the catch-all — and reports whether they let it fetch the site root. A named group is not required: under RFC 9309 §2.2.1 an open catch-all grants the same access.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Origin robots policy evaluated at `/` for PerplexityBot; review the training/search grouping separately from path access. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Absent/non-200/empty or unparseable robots data returns NA. Effective root allowance passes; a root block fails. Named groups and wildcard inheritance use the shared robots parser.
review.proposedWork: Retain origin policy scope independent of page purpose. Label the tested path. Root allowance cannot establish access to each sampled URL. Usage-control tokens must not become network impersonation probes. A publisher may intend a restriction.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Named/wildcard precedence, absent policy, root allowed with deep URL blocked and the reverse; unchanged outcome across page labels. Add token-specific legacy/control cases where relevant.

audits.title: robots.txt AI group shadowing
audits.purpose: Detects the RFC 9309 group-precedence trap: adding ANY named group for an AI product token silently voids every rule in the `User-agent: *` group for that bot. Evaluates each AI token twice — under its own merged group and under the wildcard group — with longest-match-wins and Allow-wins-on-tie, and reports three failure classes: a wildcard-protected path reopened for the bot, a named group with no rules at all, and a named group that blocks a bot the wildcard allowed.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Named robots groups compared with wildcard over rule literals, root and selected page paths, capped at 200. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Absent robots NA. Empty named groups/shadowed protections fail; a named root block can warn; no divergence passes.
review.proposedWork: Origin policy comparison with path evidence. The implementation does not sample sitemap paths despite dossier wording. Different groups can encode intent; do not label every difference unintended. Stabilize capped samples.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Intentional named overrides, empty named groups, wildcard rules, glob-derived probes, 200-plus paths and page order.

audits.title: Robots directives do not block AI indexing
audits.purpose: Robots directives — `<meta name="robots">`, per-bot meta tags and the `X-Robots-Tag` header — decide whether a page can be indexed at all and whether it can be quoted in an AI answer. A `noindex` on a content page removes it from the index AI Overviews and AI Mode draw on; `nosnippet` and `max-snippet:0` leave it indexed but unquotable.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Parsed page metadata and headers; utility-route heuristic changes noindex handling. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Empty pages NA. Non-utility noindex/none fails; snippet/archive restrictions warn; permitted directives pass.
review.proposedWork: Retain per-page policy scope with independent utility-purpose evidence. Do not attribute a named-bot directive to all consumers. Stable representative URLs must replace page-order choice.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Localized/custom utility routes, general pages, named directives, empty-body metadata, conflicting channels and reordered samples.

audits.title: RSL licensing terms are discoverable and conformant
audits.purpose: Looks for an RSL licence in all four channels the specification defines — the robots.txt `License:` directive, a `Link: rel=license` response header, an HTML `<link>`, and an inline `<script type="application/rsl+xml">` — then validates the document: its namespace, its media type, the paths its `<content url>` covers, and the enumerated attributes on every permits, prohibits, payment and amount element.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Advertised/fallback RSL documents, page inline licenses and all selected URL paths. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No candidates NA, including some invalid-advertisement-only cases. Each license is compared with every selected page. Conformance/fetch findings fail; clean documents pass.
review.proposedWork: Optional license feature. Bind a page-advertised license to its advertised population. Retain host and resource scope; a license for one page need not cover every page. Unread licenses are not proven malformed.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Independent page licenses, foreign-host content prefixes, malformed advertised URI, one unread license, fallback absence and capped/deduplicated candidates.

audits.title: Low-value URLs excluded from AI crawls
audits.purpose: AI crawlers honour path-level Disallow rules (RFC 9309), so robots.txt is the lever for keeping low-value URL spaces — carts, checkouts, site-search results, login and account pages — out of AI crawls and out of the answers built from them. This is crawl hygiene, not access control.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Observed utility routes from scanned URLs, same-host links and shared sitemap entries. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No candidates NA. All AI tokens blocked at root also returns NA. All observed families blocked pass; partial coverage warns; none fails.
review.proposedWork: Retain observed-feature scope, not hypothetical admin paths. Root block can have deeper Allow exceptions. The dossier opening still implies security protection; robots rules are not authorization. Preserve locale/mount prefixes.
review.acceptanceCriteria: No utility routes, nested/localized routes, duplicate family prefixes, root block with deep Allow, legitimate publicly useful pages and sitemap-only candidates.

audits.title: TDM-Rep declaration
audits.purpose: TDM-Rep is a W3C Community Group Final Report — explicitly not a W3C Standard — that defines a machine-readable text-and-data-mining reservation, anchored in EU DSM Directive Article 4. Its value is legal evidence of an opt-out, not agent behaviour: no major AI crawler operator documents honouring it. This audit reports what a site declares and in which direction, and never scores it either way.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: First page carrying a reservation header, otherwise root policy file, otherwise all page meta values. Grade C; experimental tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No declaration NA. Valid 0 and 1 declarations pass as reported policy; invalid values warn. Different file/meta values warn without preserving their resource scopes.
review.proposedWork: Retain optional unscored policy reporting. Keep page URL and file location attached to each value. Different permissions on different pages are not automatically contradictory; header-first selection currently hides other pages.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Two pages with different valid reservations, mixed valid/invalid headers, disjoint file locations, channel precedence on one URL and absent adoption.

audits.title: A signed agent request is not rejected for being signed
audits.purpose: Fetches the site root twice: once plainly, and once with the RFC 9421 `Signature`, `Signature-Input` and `Signature-Agent` headers a Web Bot Auth agent sends, signed with a per-scan ephemeral Ed25519 key. Reports when the signed request is refused, truncated, or answered differently without `Vary` naming the headers that changed the answer.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Unsigned and signed probes at the origin root. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Unsafe/unusable baseline NA. Signed fetch failure, selected rejection statuses or body collapse fail; negotiated auth passes; otherwise warns on differing uncached variants or passes.
review.proposedWork: Common root transport tolerance, independent of page purpose. A length/status match is not exact body equality. Failure to fetch is not proof that signature headers caused refusal. Preserve path and sample limits.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Missing signed response, auth negotiation, same-size different body, transient status changes, deep-only rules and valid Vary token handling.

audits.title: agents.json at /.well-known/agents.json
audits.purpose: agents.json (Wild Card AI, spec v0.1.0) layers agent-facing flows over OpenAPI at `/.well-known/agents.json`. No AI vendor documents consuming it, the spec never moved past v0.1.0, both of its project domains are offline and the path is absent from the IANA Well-Known URIs registry — so this check never asks a site to publish the file. It reports, with no score effect, whether what is served at that path is a real agents.json document or an HTML shell.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Optional root agents.json document. Grade C; informative tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No file/empty/non-200 NA; published HTML, malformed JSON/shape or HTML media type warns; recognized document passes.
review.proposedWork: Keep optional artifact validation unscored. Do not infer need from app/page type. Current shape validation is shallow and not an end-to-end service reachability proof.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Unadopted site, empty arrays, malformed source/flow entries, catch-all HTML and blocked artifact fetch.

audits.title: AI Catalog exists
audits.purpose: The AI catalog is the ARD discovery manifest that tells AI agents which MCP servers, agent cards, skills and API descriptions your site offers. Hugging Face's hf-discover resolves it at /.well-known/ai-catalog.json and reads its entries; without it, agents must probe endpoints to work out what your site can do.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Shared ARD reader at the well-known path plus page link/header advertisements. Grade C; informative tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Absent/HTML without advertisement fails; advertised absence warns. Malformed JSON/shape fails; empty entries warn; nonempty manifest passes.
review.proposedWork: Optional catalog feature; absence should be neutral. Preserve advertised-but-broken findings. Dossier history claims grade A while current frontmatter/code are C informative; reconcile authority before any grade move.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Unadopted site, advertised missing file, catch-all HTML, malformed manifest, empty entries and multiple page advertisements.

audits.title: AI Catalog complete metadata
audits.purpose: Consumers rank AI catalog entries on their metadata: Hugging Face's hf-discover builds its match text from each entry's description, tags, capabilities and representativeQueries. An entry with only an identifier and a type is legal ARD but is nearly unmatchable, so agents searching for what you offer will not surface it.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Host and entry metadata in the shared ARD manifest. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No readable manifest or entries NA. No indexed annotations fails; missing host display name/thin entries warn; otherwise pass.
review.proposedWork: Retain adopted-catalog population. Readable entries need not disappear with unrelated malformed data. Distinguish spec-required fields from optional metadata useful to the documented indexer.
review.acceptanceCriteria: No catalog, partial malformed entries, host-only defect, inline/linked entries, optional metadata and stable labels.

audits.title: AI Catalog entry URLs valid
audits.purpose: Every AI catalog entry either embeds its artifact inline or points at one with a url. Consumers dereference those urls to load MCP server cards, agent cards and nested catalogs, so a dead url silently truncates a whole branch of discovery and breaks any agent that trusted the manifest.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Safely resolved linked ARD entry URLs via pooled shared probes. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No manifest or no linked entries NA. All reachable pass, some warn, none fail; inline entries are skipped.
review.proposedWork: Linked-entry feature. Resolve references against the artifact location and distinguish protected, refused and unread targets from broken links. Document status handling instead of the dossier opening's blanket HTTP 200 rule.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Inline-only entries, relative references, auth-protected services, malformed/private URL, mixed probe failures and duplicate URLs.

audits.title: CORS on declared API routes
audits.purpose: CORS matters for one class of AI consumer: agent code running inside a browser origin, such as an OpenAI Apps SDK widget in an isolated iframe under a strict CSP. Server-side crawlers and MCP clients are not browsers and are unaffected. This audit reads the endpoints out of your published OpenAPI document and probes those, and applies only to sites that publish one.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Endpoints resolved by a separate /openapi.json reader and probed for CORS. Grade C; informative tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No spec/resolvable endpoints NA. Any wildcard endpoint passes; named/no headers or unread probes warn.
review.proposedWork: Browser-origin consumer only; retain informative status. One wildcard endpoint does not establish access to every API route or credentialed operation. Share artifact resolution and report per-route methods/coverage.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Mixed CORS routes, protected endpoints, exact named origins, methods/headers, unsafe targets and other spec discovery routes.

audits.title: MCP server discovery file
audits.purpose: Reports whether the site publishes an MCP discovery document at `/.well-known/mcp/servers.json` or `/.well-known/ucp`, and whether what it publishes can be parsed. Neither path is registered or specified, and no shipping MCP client is documented as fetching either, so this is reported rather than scored: a site with a working MCP server discovered by any other route is not less agent-ready for having no such file.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Root servers.json, otherwise UCP profile. Grade C; informative tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No document NA; malformed/empty declarations fail; nonempty server/service/capability lists pass.
review.proposedWork: Optional published discovery feature, unscored. UCP capabilities alone are not proof of an MCP server. First-document precedence can hide a valid alternative or an additional defective declaration.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Multiple discovery routes, commerce-only UCP, malformed server entries, catch-all HTML and unread artifacts.

audits.title: MCP endpoint functional
audits.purpose: One MCP endpoint audit: it finds the endpoint your site declares, speaks a spec-compliant JSON-RPC 2.0 initialize handshake to it, reports the capabilities the server negotiates on the wire, and checks that the tools it lists carry safety annotations.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: First endpoint from shared MCP discovery, legacy initialize and optional tools/list. Grade C; informative tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No endpoint or malformed declaration fails. Auth challenge passes; invalid reply/no capability or missing annotations warns; successful handshake passes, even if tools/list cannot be read.
review.proposedWork: Optional MCP feature; absent declaration should be NA. Consolidate reachability with the modern check without letting legacy probes penalize supported modern servers. Discovery currently treats a server-card URL as an endpoint and stops at a malformed earlier source.
review.acceptanceCriteria: No adoption, alternate valid declaration, card versus endpoint, protected server, modern-only endpoint and incomplete tools/list.

audits.title: Modern-Era Reachability Probe (server/discover)
audits.purpose: Determine, with one unauthenticated stateless POST, whether the site's MCP endpoint can be used at all by a client built on the current protocol revision (2026-07-28). Classifies the endpoint into modern / dual-era / legacy-only / deprecated-HTTP+SSE / unreachable, and extracts supportedVersions, capabilities, instructions and serverInfo from the DiscoverResult.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: First declared endpoint; discover, GET, DELETE and legacy fallback probes. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No endpoint NA; selected protocol failures fail; auth/older revision/residue warns; accepted configured revision passes.
review.proposedWork: Endpoint feature, independent of page purpose. Align source revision, negotiated protocol and consumer support before score changes. Discovery-channel limits and missing negative probes must remain visible; do not certify unobserved methods.
review.acceptanceCriteria: No declaration, protected endpoint, mixed supported revisions, missing GET/DELETE, malformed discovery and modern-only server.

audits.title: OAuth Discovery Chain Integrity (RFC 9728 → RFC 8414)
audits.purpose: Walks the full credential-free authorization discovery path an MCP client must traverse — 401 challenge, WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata, Protected Resource Metadata document, authorization server metadata — and asserts every MUST-level validation gate the client will apply. Ends before any token is requested, so it needs no credentials.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Declared endpoint challenge, resource metadata and bounded authorization-server metadata reads. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No endpoint/unreachable NA; public endpoint without PRM NA. Broken mandatory chain fails; recommended fields warn; otherwise passes.
review.proposedWork: Authorization feature, not a requirement for every MCP server. Preserve challenge status, metadata validity and sample limits; malformed advertised metadata cannot silently become legitimate public absence.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Public/no-auth, challenged missing metadata, advertised malformed metadata, alternate issuers, bounded issuer list and unsafe URL.

audits.title: The MCP endpoint validates Origin and its CORS policy matches its auth posture
audits.purpose: Sends the discover call twice — once with a throwaway `Origin`, once without — and one CORS preflight, then compares. An endpoint that reflects an arbitrary Origin into `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` while also allowing credentials has authorized every page the user visits to call it on the user’s behalf. Permissive CORS on an endpoint with no auth surface is reported and not scored.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Baseline discover, arbitrary Origin and OPTIONS at a declared endpoint. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No endpoint/baseline NA. Reflected credentialed or wildcard authenticated surfaces fail; no differentiation may warn; otherwise passes.
review.proposedWork: Endpoint/browser-origin feature. Missing Origin/preflight reads cannot prove a policy. Header tokens, bearer versus ambient credentials and legitimate same-status rejections need source-bound semantics.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Missing probes, same status with different body, explicit Authorization policy, exact allowed origin, malformed token substrings and protected baseline.

audits.title: The MCP server is listed in the official registry under a namespace this domain owns
audits.purpose: Searches the official MCP Registry for servers whose `remotes[].url` lives on this domain, classifies each listing by namespace — reverse-DNS of this domain, an individual’s GitHub account, or a third-party aggregator — and checks that the domain-control proof the reverse-DNS namespace requires is actually being served at `/.well-known/mcp-registry-auth`.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Domain/brand registry searches, matching remote domains and apex ownership proof. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No endpoint/domain NA. No listings, missing proof or third-party-only ownership can fail; other listing issues warn; otherwise passes. Failed registry fetches look like no listing.
review.proposedWork: Separate optional registry adoption from MCP endpoint existence. The dossier admits its Evidence block belongs to unrelated audits; observable registry data alone does not establish a consumer penalty. Resolve this before 7.0.0 scoring. No grade changed in this slice.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Unlisted working server, registry outage, subdomain/hosted service ownership, malformed versus absent proof, GitHub namespace and stale listing.

audits.title: Tool Contract Validity and Silent-Drop Risk
audits.purpose: Static validation of every tool definition returned by tools/list against the MUST/SHOULD-level structural rules in the 2026-07-28 tools spec — with special weight on x-mcp-header violations, which oblige conforming clients to silently remove the offending tool from the list they show the model.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Shared paginated tools/list and object tool definitions. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No endpoint/no retained tools NA. Structural mandatory failures fail, naming issues warn, otherwise passes. The gatherer drops non-object entries and returns partial lists on read failure.
review.proposedWork: Tool-definition feature. Distinguish absent capability, auth/unread listing and malformed returned entries. Report partial coverage. Recheck schema constraints before asserting every required key absent from properties invalidates all calls.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Resource-only server, malformed entries beside valid tools, failed next page, schema references/pattern properties, duplicate names and invalid header annotations.

audits.title: Tool Self-Description Coverage
audits.purpose: Counts, over the tool surface the endpoint already returned, what fraction of tools carry a description, what fraction of every input parameter carries one — walking `properties` recursively and into `items.properties` for arrays of objects — and reports the advisory ratios alongside: constrained string parameters, declared output schemas, titles and the server’s own `instructions`.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Shared tool definitions and recursive parameter descriptions, plus discover instructions. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No endpoint/tools NA. Coverage thresholds fail; stub text or absent instructions warns; otherwise passes. Truncation is reported, but unread tool entries disappear in the gatherer.
review.proposedWork: Observed tool feature. Distinguish optional instructions, required descriptions and heuristic length. Keep thresholds/claims consistent: a threshold pass cannot claim every tool is described unless coverage is 100%.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Partial/unread listing, references and nested required parameters, concise descriptions, absent optional instructions and coverage at each threshold.

audits.title: tools/list Determinism and Cache-Hint Compliance
audits.purpose: Repeatedly fetches tools/list and asserts three things the spec ties directly to agent cost and latency: caching hints are present and well-formed (ttlMs >= 0, cacheScope in {public, private}), tool ordering is stable across calls, and the tool set does not vary per connection.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Repeated paginated tools/list calls with cache metadata and definition hashes. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No initial tools NA. Cache findings fail, differences warn, otherwise passes. Later failed calls stop the loop, yet pass wording still claims all configured calls answered.
review.proposedWork: Observed tool-list feature. Require enough completed comparable calls for stability claims. Zero TTL validity and caching cost need separate treatment; expose missing/partial reads without inventing determinism.
review.acceptanceCriteria: One of three calls answered, failed later page, changing tools/order/serialization, zero TTL, private cache scope and legitimate timed updates.

audits.title: Version Downgrade Recoverability
audits.purpose: Negative-path probe that verifies the server fails correctly when handed a protocol version it does not support, and when the MCP-Protocol-Version header disagrees with the body's _meta. Both are MUST-level behaviors whose absence strands otherwise-compatible clients.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Three version probes against the first declared endpoint plus advertised revisions. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No endpoint/first unanswered probe NA. Unsupported/mismatch defects fail or warn. Missing later responses do not prevent a pass claiming mismatch rejection.
review.proposedWork: Endpoint protocol feature. Grade only responses read; authentication and unsupported-era responses need applicability before conformance claims. Separate incomplete probes from server violations.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Only first probe answered, auth challenge, protocol error inside HTTP 200, missing advertised revisions and header/body mismatch.

audits.title: OpenAPI description quality for tool-calling
audits.purpose: When an AI agent converts your OpenAPI spec into callable tools, the description fields become the prompt the LLM uses to decide when and how to call each function. A one-word description like "search" tells the model nothing about what the endpoint does, what the parameter means, or what values are valid — so the agent guesses, calls the wrong tool, or fills parameters with hallucinated values. Every operation and every parameter needs a verbose description (more than 15 characters) that explains purpose, expected input, and behavior.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Descriptions on operations and parameters gathered from a parsed spec. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No spec/checkable items NA; 90% coverage passes, 50% warns, lower fails. Length above 15 characters defines described.
review.proposedWork: Tool-conversion consumer population. Presence/length is a heuristic, not proof of quality. Report actual coverage; review reference resolution and shared path parameters.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Referenced/inherited parameters, short informative text, long boilerplate, malformed paths, multilingual descriptions and stable missing labels.

audits.title: OpenAPI has endpoints
audits.purpose: An OpenAPI spec without endpoints is like a menu with no items. AI agents need at least one path with an operation to know what actions they can perform on your site. Add your most important endpoints first.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Shared OpenAPI reader and surviving path operations. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Absent spec NA; malformed paths or no operations fail; surviving operations pass with defect notes.
review.proposedWork: Retain adopted-spec scope and partial-read semantics. Align with discovery routes and retain operation/path attribution. HTML page type must not decide applicability.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Absent/malformed/empty paths, valid operations beside bad entries, linked spec discovery and identical artifact across page labels.

audits.title: API description discoverable
audits.purpose: One discovery audit over the mechanisms that actually exist: the RFC 9727 /.well-known/api-catalog linkset, an OpenAPI document at a probed root path, and a <link rel="service-desc"> advertising one. A site with no API surface is not applicable rather than failing.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Root API catalog/spec files or the first advertised spec link on selected pages. Grade B; informative tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Any recognized catalog/spec passes; malformed JSON spec or unverifiable link warns; no API surface NA. YAML and JSON absence/defect handling differ.
review.proposedWork: Optional API discovery feature, not a page-purpose requirement. Use the same discovered artifact set as content audits; current content readers do not follow every discovery route. Resolve page-relative links against their page.
review.acceptanceCriteria: No API, catalog-only, linked/YAML specs, malformed artifacts, multiple advertisements, page-relative URL and unread advertised target.

audits.title: OpenAPI has operationIds
audits.purpose: AI agents use operationIds as stable function names when calling your API. Without unique operationIds, agents must guess endpoint names from paths, leading to ambiguity and errors. An operationId that is not a legal function name (spaces, punctuation, or more than 64 characters) cannot be registered as a tool at all.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Operation IDs in the shared spec reader. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Absent spec or empty operation set NA; malformed paths/illegal names fail; missing/duplicate IDs warn; valid IDs pass.
review.proposedWork: Feature scope is declared operations. Tool-name restrictions need the documented converter population; an OpenAPI ID need not be a universal vendor tool name. Keep unread entries separate.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Missing/duplicate/illegal IDs, multiple converters, malformed paths with valid survivors and no operations.

audits.title: OpenAPI request/response schemas
audits.purpose: Without request/response schemas, AI agents must guess the data format for your endpoints. This leads to malformed requests and failed API calls. Define JSON schemas for all request bodies and responses.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Request/response schema presence across surviving operations. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Absent spec/empty operations NA; malformed paths fail. Full coverage passes, at least half warns, lower coverage fails.
review.proposedWork: Operation feature; distinguish methods needing bodies and responses carrying content. References and legitimate no-content responses must not become missing schemas. The first content-bearing response currently ends the search.
review.acceptanceCriteria: 204 responses, bodyless writes, references, multiple response orderings and malformed entries beside valid operations.

audits.title: OpenAPI servers array valid
audits.purpose: Without a servers array, AI agents do not know the base URL for your API. They cannot construct valid request URLs, rendering the entire spec unusable. Add at least your production server URL.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: First nonempty URL in the spec servers array and a shared GET probe. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No spec NA. Missing servers/URL fails; reachable first server passes; unreachable or other status warns.
review.proposedWork: Optional API feature. Review spec defaults, relative URLs, variables and version-specific server models before requiring an absolute top-level server. One sampled server cannot certify every declared server.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Relative/default servers, variables, Swagger versus OpenAPI, multiple servers, unsafe URL and unavailable probe.

audits.title: Site search reachable by agents
audits.purpose: A declared search endpoint lets an AI agent find specific content on your site without crawling every page. This audit covers both halves of that declaration: the Schema.org SearchAction URL template, and a GET search operation in your OpenAPI spec — and it probes the template rather than trusting it.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: SearchAction from selected pages or a GET search operation in OpenAPI. Grade C; informative tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Verified result-bearing SearchAction or matching operation passes; defective/gated/no-action WebSite warns; no declaration fails.
review.proposedWork: Optional search feature. A WebSite node alone does not imply site search. A valid empty result set for the arbitrary query `test` is not proof of a defective endpoint. Keep declaration and runtime proof distinct.
review.acceptanceCriteria: No search, legitimate zero results, advertised malformed template, relative URL, multiple actions and OpenAPI-only declaration.

audits.title: WebMCP declarative form tools
audits.purpose: WebMCP's Declarative API turns an HTML <form> into an agent-callable tool: add toolname and tooldescription and the browser synthesizes a JSON Schema from the form's controls, which an in-browser agent can discover and invoke without any JavaScript. toolname is what registers the tool — a description on its own registers nothing.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: All forms across selected pages plus declarative WebMCP attributes. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No forms/no annotation NA. Any adoption makes all forms the denominator; none named fails, partial names/descriptions warn, all complete pass.
review.proposedWork: Gate at the adopted form, not the whole site. A search form exposing a tool must not force a newsletter or payment form on another page to adopt. Grade B remains unchanged.
review.acceptanceCriteria: One complete adopted form beside an ordinary form, malformed adopted form, duplicate names per page, description gaps and no adoption.

audits.title: WebMCP registered tools
audits.purpose: WebMCP lets a page register agent-callable tools at runtime through navigator.modelContext, which is what Chrome exposes to an in-browser agent and what Lighthouse reports as "Registered WebMCP tools". This scanner has no JavaScript runtime, so it reports the registrations visible in the served document and treats silence as unknown rather than as absence — which is why it is experimental and never scores.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Inline script patterns and declarative form markers across pages. Grade B; experimental tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Observed tool names pass; API reference without names warns; declarative-only or no static signal NA.
review.proposedWork: Retain experimental static-observation scope. Source text does not prove runtime registration. Keep page/name associations; external bundles and runtime conditions remain unobserved.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Unexecuted source, external script, per-page duplicate names, declarative-only forms, multiple pages and absent feature.

audits.title: ACP link-surface completeness
audits.purpose: Verifies the merchant can populate the `links` array that every ACP CheckoutSession response is required to carry, by resolving each of the 8 enum link types to a stable, HTTPS, no-JS-required, non-soft-404 URL, on any domain, as an HTML page or a PDF.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Links across selected pages plus policy URL validation. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No pages/anchors NA. Otherwise checks eight ACP link types; missing hard gates fail, partial set warns, all pass.
review.proposedWork: Require independent ACP/merchant evidence. Any ordinary anchor currently activates checkout obligations on non-commerce sites. Bind each claim to the protocol/version and observed checkout surface.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Informational site with links, merchant without ACP adoption, actual ACP surface, external/PDF policies and unread target.

audits.title: Shopping agents can fetch the commerce paths
audits.purpose: Issues paired requests to the homepage, sampled product pages, the cart and the linked policy pages with a browser User-Agent and with the ChatGPT-User and OAI-SearchBot User-Agents, detecting WAF blocks, challenge interstitials and stub pages that a robots.txt-only audit cannot see. Reads the OpenAI robots.txt tokens separately, so opting out of training while staying in search is reported as the deliberate posture it is.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Root, first selected URLs labeled PDPs, guessed cart and discovered policy links. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No pages/unreachable cart or no comparable baselines NA; any access delta/path disallow fails; otherwise passes.
review.proposedWork: Select proven commerce URLs; arbitrary pages are not PDPs. Preserve same-URL baseline comparison, intentional crawler policy and incomplete probe coverage. Do not claim both agents matched every target from partial pairs.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Non-commerce site, real product outside default paths, partial probes, intentional training block and custom cart URL.

audits.title: Buyable Variant Resolution
audits.purpose: Finds product pages that offer a shopper a size or colour choice but publish no per-variant purchasable identifier with its own price and availability, so an agent cannot turn "the blue one in medium" into a line item. Variants are established from the rendered HTML, then the structured data is required to resolve them.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `product`; variant controls/groups and product fields on the first three pages. Grade B.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: no variant feature NA; any failure fails, else warnings warn, otherwise passes. The sample cap depends on input order.
review.proposedWork: variant feature in supported commerce pages; deterministic bounded selection and explicit omitted coverage. Keep group and buyable-variant identity distinct. A passing sampled set cannot claim full input coverage.
review.acceptanceCriteria: no variants, real selector versus decorative options, unresolved variant identity, group/per-variant data, four-plus pages and permutations.

audits.title: Cart Handoff Reachability
audits.purpose: Reads the storefront cart and checkout paths — the URL an agent hands a buyer to, whether through an ACP `continue_url` or a computer-use agent driving the storefront — as a browser and as ChatGPT-User, and reports an account wall, a bot challenge on the checkout document, or a hard block. Read-only: every request is a GET, nothing is ever added to a cart.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Platform fingerprint and guessed cart/checkout paths with browser/agent probes. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No platform/no answers NA; known platform/no answers fails. Blocks/account walls fail, JS-only warns, otherwise passes.
review.proposedWork: Observed cart/handoff feature. A guessed path is not a published continue_url; a catalog-only storefront may have no cart. Missing paired response and server errors must not count as successful handoff.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Catalog-only platform, custom/advertised cart, 500 or partial probe, legitimate account-required flow, catch-all HTML and absence.

audits.title: Checkout-eligible offer field mapping
audits.purpose: Audits each PDP against the exact required-and-conditional field set of the OpenAI product feed spec, including its character caps and its conditional triggers, so the merchant learns which rows will be rejected before uploading a feed.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `product`; first product plus field-verification evidence from the selected sample. Grade A for the documented feed path.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: no product NA; mapping problems fail, ambiguity warns, valid passes. Dossier says every PDP; implementation picks one.
review.proposedWork: explicitly supported commerce/feed population with per-product mapping. Existing schema alone must not imply enrollment in an optional feed. Review whether the scored claim is applicable or a mapping preview before widening it.
review.acceptanceCriteria: unenrolled store, valid/invalid mappings, ambiguous field ownership, two unequal PDPs, shared field-verification evidence and deterministic sample order.

audits.title: Landed-cost and returns machine readability
audits.purpose: Requires structured, agent-parsable shipping cost, handling and transit times, and a return window expressed as an integer — the exact inputs an agent needs to rank offers and the exact fields the ACP checkout session must compute.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `product`; first Offer or offers object, shipping fields and return policy from the offer or elsewhere in the sample. Grade A.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: no offer NA; problems fail, link-only warns, valid passes. Later offers are not assessed; arbitrary policy fallback lacks ownership.
review.proposedWork: present offer, per-offer coverage, correctly inherited merchant policy. Do not import another product's or merchant's policy.
review.acceptanceCriteria: absent versus defective offer, two offers with different shipping, linked policy, correct Organization inheritance, unrelated policy and page order.

audits.title: Offer schema on pricing pages
audits.purpose: AI agents use Offer schema to answer pricing queries with exact numbers. Without price and priceCurrency in structured data, agents must scrape and guess pricing from page text, which often produces inaccurate or outdated results in AI-generated comparisons.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `product`; Offer/AggregateOffer or offers properties and price/currency on each selected page. Grade A.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: empty NA; all pages covered pass, some warn, none fail.
review.proposedWork: confirmed buyable-product purpose, independent of schema. Bind offers to the primary product; distinguish presence from content validation and support the documented aggregate-offer shape.
review.acceptanceCriteria: product without schema, non-buyable product, related offer, AggregateOffer, malformed present offer and mixed product coverage.

audits.title: Offer Truth Consistency
audits.purpose: Reconciles the Offer in a product page’s structured data against what the same page actually renders: the price, the currency, whether the item can be bought, whether the offer window has closed, and whether two Product nodes describing the same URL disagree. Every rule is a value comparison, not a presence check, and extraction is confined to the product region so a related-products carousel cannot fire it.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `product`; offers and visible product-region price, currency and availability on the first three pages. Grade B.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: contradictions fail, warnings warn, otherwise passes; no checked data warns. Missing rendered prices can produce a claim about client rendering.
review.proposedWork: present offer/visible-price feature with deterministic bounded coverage. A missing fetched price does not prove JavaScript-only rendering or what every crawler sees. Report the observation and unread state.
review.acceptanceCriteria: matching/conflicting price, unrelated cards, localization, missing visible price, no offer, multiple offers and four-plus page permutations.

audits.title: Product identifiers (GTIN/UPC/MPN)
audits.purpose: AI agents use unique identifiers like GTIN, UPC, or MPN to de-duplicate products across different sources and confirm they are looking at the exact item the user wants. Without them, agents may confuse similar products or fail to find specific pricing.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `product`; flattened products and identifiers from the first product/offers. Grade A.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: no product fails; any accepted identifier on the first product passes; otherwise fails.
review.proposedWork: primary-product identity with per-product coverage. Review identifier alternatives and legitimate unassigned identifiers; do not require a fabricated GTIN or let a related product satisfy the page.
review.acceptanceCriteria: missing Product, SKU/MPN/GTIN alternatives, no assigned GTIN, related cards, multiple product entities and mixed PDPs.

audits.title: Product transactional certainty
audits.purpose: AI shopping assistants need more than a product name and price to make an authoritative recommendation: they must know whether the item is in stock, how long the quoted price is valid, and what the return policy is before they commit a user to a purchase. A Product schema that only carries name and price forces agents to guess at availability, quote potentially stale prices, and stay silent on returns — all of which erode transactional certainty in agentic commerce flows. Complete your Offer with availability, priceValidUntil, and a valid price + priceCurrency pair, and attach hasMerchantReturnPolicy to the Product or Offer.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `product`; existing products/offers with availability, validity date, price pair and returns policy. Grade A.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: no products NA; no offers fails; best product passes at four factors, warns at two, else fails. Fields can come from different offers.
review.proposedWork: present transaction feature. Judge coherent offers instead of combining facts from different transactions. Review validity-date and other optional-field requirements against the consumer's supported path.
review.acceptanceCriteria: no artifact, broken offer, split facts across conflicting offers, unexpired/no-expiry price, variant offers and mixed products.

audits.title: About page with credentials
audits.purpose: AI engines crawl your about page to build an organizational authority profile. Without an about page containing team credentials, expertise, and experience details, agents cannot assess your organization's authority, reducing your content's trust score in AI-generated recommendations.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: First about-like cached page or root-path probe; English credential words in raw HTML. Grade C; informative tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No candidate fails; two keywords pass, one or none warn.
review.proposedWork: Site-identity advisory with language and probe limits. Missing conventional paths do not establish no about page; words in scripts do not establish credentials. Keep informational status.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Localized linked about page, catch-all shell, unavailable probe, keyword in script and equivalent identity content under another route.

audits.title: Author page exists
audits.purpose: AI engines follow author page links to verify credentials and build author expertise profiles. A dedicated author page strengthens E-E-A-T signals.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `content`; JSON-LD author URLs and author links; safe probe via the author gatherer. Grade C, informative.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: no pages/links fails; probes only the first collected URL. Non-200 and failed reads collapse into failure.
review.proposedWork: present author-link feature, distinct missing/unread/broken states and explicit bounded link coverage. Retain URL safety and shared fetches.
review.acceptanceCriteria: no link, two authors with different outcomes, URL order, unsafe URL, refused redirect, timeout, real 404 and successful shared author link.

audits.title: Author schema with sameAs
audits.purpose: AI RAG systems cross-reference author identity across platforms via sameAs URLs. Without external profile links, agents cannot verify author expertise.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `content`; Person/article-author sameAs values beginning with HTTP across all selected pages. Grade C, informative.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: first matching value passes; none fails, including empty input. Does not prove an external author profile.
review.proposedWork: optional linked-author feature with entity ownership; distinguish absent enrichment from a defective supplied link. Keep unscored.
review.acceptanceCriteria: unrelated Person, same-site URL, malformed link, author reference, no authorship and different author-link coverage across articles.

audits.title: Brand name in body text
audits.purpose: AI engines build entity graphs by matching Organization schema names to in-content mentions. If your brand name only appears in schema but not body text, agents cannot associate your content with your entity.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Names from JSON-LD plus first-page site name; body text on any page. Grade C; informative tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Empty pages fail; no name warns; any candidate-name mention passes; none fail.
review.proposedWork: Entity-specific identity advisory. Article/WebPage names are not necessarily brands. Bind claimed publisher to matching text and avoid requiring every page to repeat it.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Article title as name, third-party organization, multilingual boundary matching, missing identity data and stable representative URL.

audits.title: Chunk-boundary referent integrity
audits.purpose: Splits the page into heading-led chunks, the way a retriever does, and checks each one for the three ways a chunk loses its meaning when it arrives alone: opening on a demonstrative with no referent, never naming the page's subject, and pointing at a position in the document ("as described above") that a retrieved chunk no longer has.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: First-page H2/H3 chunks and entity/anaphora/positional-reference heuristics. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No page/chunks NA. Coverage thresholds choose fail/warn/pass; pass text can say every chunk despite a threshold below 100%.
review.proposedWork: Heading-led retrieval feature in the documented language/population. A configurable retrieval strategy is not universal. Bind the entry explicitly or adopt reviewed per-page aggregation; expose measured fractions.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Non-English text, short standalone sections, no entity metadata, one failing chunk above pass threshold and page order.

audits.title: Comparison tables present
audits.purpose: AI answer engines extract structured table data to generate comparison answers. Add HTML tables to your content where appropriate.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current category/product/content; any `<table>` in any selected page. Grade C, informative.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: any table passes; none fails, including empty input. Does not establish comparison intent or distinguish layout tables.
review.proposedWork: comparison feature; no comparison NA. Keep unscored. A homepage comparison is a candidate for scope expansion, not automatic scoring permission.
review.acceptanceCriteria: no comparison, layout table, real comparison with/without a table, homepage feature, multiple pages and accessible alternative representations.

audits.title: Content answers without click-through
audits.purpose: AI answer engines skip teaser content that gates answers behind sign-ups or downloads. Provide substantive answers directly on the page.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Teaser phrases across pages; otherwise word count of the first non-root/non-XML page. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Two phrase patterns on a page fail; short chosen page warns; unread text NA; otherwise pass. Empty sample fails.
review.proposedWork: Feature/purpose eligibility must distinguish listing teasers from withheld article answers. Readability belongs to the judged page, not unrelated scan evidence. Stable sampling replaces first eligible choice.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Product/category cards, full article with legitimate download link, short utility page, mixed readable/unread pages and reorder.

audits.title: Core Open Graph tags
audits.purpose: Link-preview crawlers — facebookexternalhit and Slack's unfurler are documented by name — read og:title, og:description, og:image and og:url to build the card shown when your page is shared, and Google names og:site_name as one input to the site name on a result. This audit scores those Open Graph properties; the Twitter Card tags it also reports are informational only, because every content-bearing twitter:* tag falls back to its og:* counterpart.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Core OG metadata and optional site name on the first page; Twitter tags reported only. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: All core tags plus site name pass; partial core/missing site name warn; no core tags or pages fail.
review.proposedWork: Common share-preview population with an explicit current entry-page dossier limit. Keep optional site name separate from core fields. Review wider page aggregation before changing it.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Empty sample, later-page defect, placeholders, multiple OG images, optional site name and stable entry identity.

audits.title: Dates on content pages
audits.purpose: Date extractors read the byline date off a content page from <time datetime>, JSON-LD datePublished/dateModified, article:*_time meta tags or a clearly labelled visible date; a page carrying none of them has no date any downstream consumer can attach to it. A modification date (or a visible "last updated" label with a date beside it) is the full signal; a publication date alone is a partial one.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `content`; helper excludes XML only. Reads modified/published signals in markup and visible text. Grade A.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: any modified signal passes; otherwise any publication date warns; none fails. No candidates NA. Dossier states this best-signal rule.
review.proposedWork: positive article purpose. Change the dossier's aggregation contract before replacing the best-signal rule with page coverage. Review overlap with publication-date/last-modified-schema and unchanged articles.
review.acceptanceCriteria: privacy/contact, article without schema, publication-only article, unrelated footer dates, mixed date coverage and stable provenance.

audits.title: Descriptive URL slugs
audits.purpose: AI engines use URL text as a content signal. Descriptive slugs help agents understand page topics before fetching the content.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Bad-slug patterns against each full page URL. Grade C; informative tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No pages fail; none bad pass, some bad warn, all bad fail.
review.proposedWork: Keep unscored URL advice. Do not infer page purpose or defect from an identifier alone. Match path segments deliberately and stabilize affected URLs.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Valid ID-based resource, query-only differences, non-Latin slugs, encoded paths, empty sample and order.

audits.title: Definition markup on definitional pages
audits.purpose: HTML-AAM maps <dfn> and <dt>/<dd> to the term and definition roles, and WHATWG requires the definition to sit alongside the term it defines, so the pairing survives extraction intact. No consumer is documented as acting on that mapping, and prose definitions are read perfectly well, so this is reported as upside on pages that already answer a definitional question — never as a defect.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `content`; helper selects definition intent from structural markup or lexical patterns, then assesses markup/prose. Unknown languages fall back to English patterns. Grade C, informative.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: no candidate NA; all marked passes, otherwise warns. Ordinary prose definitions do not fail.
review.proposedWork: definition feature, not every article. Preserve the existing absence and advisory rules; review widening beyond `content` against the dossier.
review.acceptanceCriteria: no definition intent, valid prose, definition list/markup, definition on a general page, unsupported languages and stable representative URLs.

audits.title: External citations
audits.purpose: Linking to authoritative sources signals expertise. AI RAG systems cross-reference your citations to validate claims and assess content quality.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `content`; all external anchors across pages, including site chrome. Grade B derives from measured citation-bearing content.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: any page with two links passes; any link warns; otherwise fails, including empty input. Representative URL can be unrelated.
review.proposedWork: supported editorial content, with citations in its body. Dossier already asks for chrome/paid-link exclusions, deduplication and page coverage. A two-link threshold is an implementation heuristic, not proof of authority.
review.acceptanceCriteria: footer social links, repeated URLs, paid links, own asset hosts, true citations, unsupported page purposes and mixed article coverage.

audits.title: Extractor survival recall
audits.purpose: Names the spans that carry the page's facts — the `h1`, each section's opening sentences, every `caption`, `dt` and `th`, and the structured-data strings the prose repeats — then runs the page through `@mozilla/readability` and through a Firecrawl/Jina-style stripper and reports which spans did not survive, and what dropped them.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: First-page key spans against Readability and an aggressive local extractor. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No page/spans NA; minimum recall chooses fail/warn/pass. Pass can claim all spans despite partial recall.
review.proposedWork: Explicit extraction experiment on one page, not proof about every agent. Preserve extractor identity, supported content population and actual retained counts; apply common scope only after dossier/sample revision.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Application/utility page, partial recall at pass threshold, hidden spans, missing extractor output and reordered pages.

audits.title: FAQ sections present
audits.purpose: AI answer engines like Perplexity extract FAQ-structured content with higher confidence for direct answers. FAQ sections with clear question headings are the top extraction target for "People Also Ask" results and conversational AI responses.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: FAQ schema, heading/summary text and FAQ-like class/id markers across pages. Grade C; informative tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Any matching page passes immediately; no match or no pages fails.
review.proposedWork: Optional FAQ presence advisory. Do not require FAQs on every site or equate a class token with readable answers. Stable sample evidence must name what was observed.
review.acceptanceCriteria: No FAQ purpose, FAQ label without answers, translated labels, class false positives and multiple matching pages.

audits.title: First paragraph answers primary question
audits.purpose: AI search engines score the first paragraph highest for extractive QA. Preamble text like "In this article" or "Welcome" wastes this prime position, causing agents to extract low-value content as your page's representative answer.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `content`; first page accepted by the imported article helper, which only excludes XML. Reads a substantive paragraph. Grade C.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: no accepted page NA; first paragraph length, English sentence pattern and weak-opener patterns decide the sample verdict.
review.proposedWork: positive article/answer purpose; per-page assessment. English patterns need an explicit language limit. Keep advisory status.
review.acceptanceCriteria: contact/privacy HTML, XML, non-English article, no paragraph, good and weak openings in reversed samples, non-article answer features.

audits.title: Last modified date in schema
audits.purpose: AI engines use dateModified in JSON-LD to determine content freshness. Content that shows recent updates is prioritized over stale content.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `content`; Article-family/WebPage dateModified and datePublished fields. Grade B.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: first modified date differing from published passes; equal warns immediately; no date fails, including empty input.
review.proposedWork: article revision or supplied metadata feature with explicit absence rules. No fabricated update dates. Distinguish malformed dates from unchanged content and remove first-node/page severity dependence.
review.acceptanceCriteria: equal/different dates in reversed nodes/pages, invalid date strings, no revision, general WebPage and partial article coverage.

audits.title: Meta author present
audits.purpose: AI agents use the meta author tag to attribute content to a specific person or organization for E-E-A-T scoring. Without it, your content appears authorless, which reduces trust signals in AI ranking systems that prioritize named expertise.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `content`; first page's meta author. Grade C, informative.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: nonempty first value passes; otherwise fails, including empty input. Ignores other selected pages.
review.proposedWork: authorship feature or supported article purpose, per-page evidence and no applicable page NA. Retain grade C; do not imply a required crawler signal.
review.acceptanceCriteria: general/privacy pages, article without meta author but another valid author representation, mixed bylines, empty input and page permutations.

audits.title: Meta description quality
audits.purpose: Google may reproduce <meta name="description"> verbatim as the snippet for a page when it describes the page better than the body text does, and the same snippet pipeline feeds AI Overviews and AI Mode source cards. This audit checks the properties Google documents: the tag is present, it is a usable length, it reads as prose rather than a keyword string, and it actually describes this page.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Description, title and H1 of the first selected page. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Absent description fails, length/prose/topic heuristics warn, otherwise passes; empty pages fail.
review.proposedWork: Common page metadata, with current first-page limit explicit in the dossier. Revise that scope deliberately or bind an explicit entry identity; never silently let reorder choose it. Length and token overlap are heuristics.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Mixed descriptions and permutations, empty sample, non-English prose, synonyms with no shared term and utility-page population.

audits.title: Named author attribution
audits.purpose: AI systems assign higher confidence to content from named experts. Generic authors like "Staff" or "Admin" reduce trust scoring because agents cannot verify expertise.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `content`; author objects, meta author or visible author/byline markers across pages. Grade C, informative.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: first qualifying name passes; none fails, including empty input. Generic-name exclusions can reject real collective authors.
review.proposedWork: bind authorship to each eligible article; do not require a byline on generic content or invent a penalty for organizational authors.
review.acceptanceCriteria: real person/organization authors, staff byline, unrelated footer name, no article, missing byline and mixed article coverage.

audits.title: og:image:alt present
audits.purpose: AI agents cannot process images directly and rely on og:image:alt text to understand your page's visual content. Without alt text, the OG image is invisible to text-based AI systems that generate answers and summaries about your page.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: First-page og:image and og:image:alt. Grade C; informative tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No image warns despite not-applicable wording; image with alt passes, image without alt fails.
review.proposedWork: Optional adopted image metadata; no image NA. Keep informative. Match alt with the corresponding image rather than flattening multi-image properties.
review.acceptanceCriteria: No image/pages, multiple images with partial alt, blank alt, later-page image and bounded text.

audits.title: og:type set and appropriate
audits.purpose: AI agents use og:type to classify page content as either a website, article, product, or other entity type. Without it, agents default to treating the page as generic content, missing opportunities for type-specific handling like article freshness scoring.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: First-page og:type plus URL substring article heuristic. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Missing/empty sample fails; blog-like path with non-article type warns; any other nonempty value passes.
review.proposedWork: Use independent purpose evidence instead of `/blog`, `/post` or `/article` substrings. A blog index is not necessarily an article. Limit claims to the documented preview consumer.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Blog index, posting form, article outside blog paths, invalid type, missing tag and reordered page sample.

audits.title: Publication date visible
audits.purpose: AI engines use visible dates to assess content freshness. Undated content is deprioritized for recency-weighted queries.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `content`; its own XML-exclusion helper accepts other HTML as articles. Reads structured or visible dates. Grade B.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: any qualifying date passes the sample; none fails; no candidates NA.
review.proposedWork: shared positive article evidence and per-article provenance. Review overlap with dates-on-content before changing denominator/aggregation.
review.acceptanceCriteria: privacy/contact, XML, publication versus footer/update dates, missing schema, mixed coverage and stable affected URLs.

audits.title: Question-formatted headings
audits.purpose: AI answer engines directly match user questions to heading text. Question-formatted headings (ending with "?") are the primary signal AI systems use to identify which section answers a specific query.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: H2/H3 headings ending with a question mark across the sample. Grade C; informative tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Two or more pass, one warns, zero/empty fails; URL is the first page.
review.proposedWork: Optional writing-style advisory, not a general page obligation. Do not let unrelated pages pool counts into a page-quality claim. Keep grade C and name the actual heading population.
review.acceptanceCriteria: No heading/question feature, one question on each of two pages, translated punctuation, rhetorical heading and source URL.

audits.title: Review/testimonial signals
audits.purpose: Google parses schema.org Review/AggregateRating to render review rich results, and attributed quotations are the best-measured lever in the GEO literature. This audit passes on machine-readable social proof — review structured data, or quotations carried in <blockquote> with attribution — and warns when review UI is on the page but nothing machine-readable is behind it.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current homepage/product; attributed quotations, review markup and widgets across selected pages. Grade B.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: empty NA; any strong signal passes, weak signal warns, none fails. One outer gate covers two different populations.
review.proposedWork: dossier permits attributed quotation on any scanned page, but review vocabulary only on homepage/product. Use branch-specific applicability with one audit weight; do not expose both to all page purposes.
review.acceptanceCriteria: attributed article quotation, unsupported review widget context, mixed page purposes, review-schema overlap and independent branch absence.

audits.title: Section split-risk profile
audits.purpose: Counts each `h2`/`h3` section with a real BPE tokenizer and reports the four ways a page chunks badly: sections over the 512-token window (each producing headless tail chunks), a long page with no headings to cut on, sections too thin to embed distinctly, and single tables or lists whose serialization exceeds the window on its own.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: First main/article of first page; H2/H3 sections against a fixed token window. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No page/short text NA; fewer than two H2s forces blob score zero; thresholds and atomic splits choose fail/warn/pass.
review.proposedWork: Long-section feature under a named retrieval strategy. One valid section or many H3s must not become a claim that there are no headings. Keep token denominator and nested-section accounting explicit.
review.acceptanceCriteria: One H2, H3-only structure, unheaded intro, nested wrappers, atomic tables/lists, multilingual token counts and short pages.

audits.title: Site-wide passage uniqueness ratio
audits.purpose: Measures two things no single-page check can see: what share of each page’s sentences are its own rather than repeated across its siblings, and which pages are near-duplicates of each other at five-gram Jaccard 0.9 or above. Near-duplicate pages that all name themselves canonical compete against each other for one slot.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Extractable sentences and shingle overlap across selected pages, with canonical clusters. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Insufficient readable pages NA; unresolved duplicates or low median fail; low outliers warn; otherwise passes.
review.proposedWork: Cross-page sample metric, not a census. Canonical equivalence, legal repeated text and sample composition matter. The dossier mentions alternate-content divergence absent from the body; keep that claim deferred.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Query/canonical aliases, necessary repeated policy text, unrelated page purposes, unread members, clustering order and even-sized median.

audits.title: Snippet-gate coverage analysis
audits.purpose: Computes the site's effective snippet permissions per crawler — merging <meta name="robots">, per-bot meta tags, and X-Robots-Tag response headers — then measures those permissions against the page's actual answer content: is max-snippet numerically smaller than the primary answer span, and does data-nosnippet coverage overlap the answer span, the FAQ answers, or the main-content tables. Reports the specific suppressed text, not just the directive.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: First-page directives, main text and candidate answer spans. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No page/main text NA; blocked snippets/suppressed spans/budget findings fail; minor subtree suppression warns; otherwise passes.
review.proposedWork: Per-page snippet permission and answer-feature measurement. An intentional snippet restriction is policy, not necessarily misconfiguration. The dossier calls it site-wide while only one page contributes.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Different page permissions, bot-specific rules, protected content, no answer spans, partial data-nosnippet and stable entry identity.

audits.title: Specific numbers and data points
audits.purpose: AI engines prefer answers with concrete data points over vague statements. Include specific numbers, percentages, and metrics in your content.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Numeric patterns in main text across selected pages. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Any matching page passes; no numeric match/empty sample fails, attributed to the first page.
review.proposedWork: Restrict the empirical claim to content where quantitative facts are relevant. A privacy/contact or qualitative explanation must not invent statistics. Preserve unsupported populations unscored pending evidence.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Qualitative versus quantitative pages, product price versus unrelated date, locale number formats, boilerplate numbers and matching-page attribution.

audits.title: Tables survive conversion to markdown
audits.purpose: Converts every main-content table to GFM markdown — the representation an answer engine’s reader emits — reads it back, and diffs it cell for cell against the source grid. Reports every cell lost or displaced by coordinate, plus the tables whose numbers carry no header and whose units live only in the caption.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Eligible top-level main-content tables on the first page; local grid/Markdown conversion. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No page/data table NA; corrupting number/unit findings or low survival fail; other loss/shape findings warn; otherwise passes.
review.proposedWork: Data-table feature regardless of page label. Name the simulated serializer and its limits. Captions can carry valid units; layout tables and nested structures need supported selection rules.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Table on later page, layout table, spanning cells, caption units, escaping pipes/newlines and comparison with actual documented converter behavior.

audits.title: Text-fragment citation addressability
audits.purpose: Determines whether a citing surface can construct a working `#:~:text=` deep link to the page's actual answer sentences. Hard-fails on the documented `Document-Policy: force-load-at-top` opt-out header, then simulates the spec's matching algorithm over the parsed DOM to prove each candidate answer span is (a) contained in a single block-level element, (b) unambiguous or disambiguable with a same-block prefix/suffix, and (c) free of characters that break normalization. Outputs the working fragment URLs as a fix artifact.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: First-page document policy and heading/definition/FAQ answer spans. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No page/spans NA, except force-load-at-top fails before candidate detection. Broken simulated match fails; normalization hazards warn; otherwise passes.
review.proposedWork: Answer-span feature with explicit browser simulation limits. Scope the opt-out to the relevant resource; no candidate should not become a manufactured citation requirement. Do not claim browser execution from static matching.
review.acceptanceCriteria: No spans with opt-out, multi-block ranges, repeated text, hidden candidates, normalization and later-page defects.

audits.title: Trust and evidence signals on homepage
audits.purpose: A 252,000-trial controlled study across six LLMs (arXiv 2605.25517) measured two page factors that shift which source an AI answer engine cites: quantified social proof (OR 2.14, significant in 4 of 6 models) and claims paired with evidence (OR 2.09, 5 of 6 models).
