The runner strips stylesheets and does not execute JS. Preserve these coverage limits and stabilize URL/selector evidence.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Duplicate referenced ID, duplicate unreferenced ID, ambiguity alongside a passing page and stable review status. Also test all page labels, mixed pass/incomplete/missing results and permutations through the shared runner.

audits.title: First-contact consent gate: cost to get past it
audits.purpose: Reports the cold-session consent layer an agent meets before any task work: whether the primary content exists in the served HTML behind it, whether the accept and reject controls carry accessible names and live in the top document rather than a cross-origin iframe, whether main content is hidden from the accessibility tree while the layer is open, and how many clicks a refusal costs. Diagnostic only — it never moves the score.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Detected consent gates across pages, but only first detected gate judged. Grade C; informative tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No static platform NA with an overly broad no-gate claim; defects warn; otherwise passes. Zero refusal controls can still pass.
review.proposedWork: Optional detected-gate advisory. Runtime gate absence remains unknown. Judge each observed gate; distinguish missing refusal control from zero-cost refusal. Keep cross-origin extraction limits explicit.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Multiple different gates, no refusal control, runtime-only platform, valid labeled choices and page order.

audits.title: Form backend actionability
audits.purpose: Autonomous agents fill forms by reading the DOM directly — they cannot see placeholders rendered visually or guess what a custom div-based widget expects. Fields without a native element, a name attribute, an explicit label (label[for], wrapping label, aria-label, or aria-labelledby), or a standard autocomplete attribute for identity data (email, phone, name, address) force agents to guess, producing failed or incorrect submissions. Keep every fillable field a native input/select/textarea with a name, an explicit label and standard autocomplete tokens.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Native and simulated fields inside forms; names, label markers and expected autofill. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No fillable fields NA; at least 90% pass, at least half warn, lower fail.
review.proposedWork: Field feature, not page type. Label references must resolve and contain text; disabled/hidden/external form-owned fields need proper population. Pooling many good forms can hide one unusable form.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Broken/empty label reference, disabled field, form attribute ownership, mixed forms/pages and exact coverage messages.

audits.title: Form Autofill Token Coverage
audits.purpose: Per-form score for whether every field an agent must populate carries the machine-readable identity an agent needs: a stable name/id, a correct input type, a WHATWG autocomplete token when the field maps to a standard autofill concept, programmatic constraints, and error wiring via aria-invalid/aria-describedby. Scored as covered-fields / autofillable-fields per form.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Autofill candidates, visual required markers and message wiring across forms/pages. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No forms/no applicable concepts NA; full coverage passes, zero coverage fails, partial/side issues warn.
review.proposedWork: Per-field feature, with query-form exclusion. Dossier says per-form while source pools counts. Keep constraints and error findings tied to the same field/page; no field should acquire identity obligations from a vague name.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Search/store-locator forms, custom labels/locales, mismatched token/type, separate failing form and stable URL.

audits.title: Form fields wired to their validation messages
audits.purpose: An agent filling a form reads the accessibility tree, where a message is attached to a field by aria-errormessage or aria-describedby. Fields the server rendered as aria-invalid are checked directly; where a page carries no invalid state — the normal case on a GET, since error markup is injected after a failed submit — the required fields are checked instead, because those are the ones that can fail.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Resolvable message references on invalid fields, otherwise required fields, across pages. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No relevant fields NA; all linked pass, some warn, none fail.
review.proposedWork: Validation feature. One invalid field currently changes the population for every other page; choose state/population per form/page. A GET cannot prove runtime validation messages. Native validation is not inherently broken.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Invalid field on one page plus required fields elsewhere, native constraint messages, stale/hidden references and mixed order.

audits.title: Forms work without JavaScript
audits.purpose: Many AI agents do not execute JavaScript, so forms that rely on JS for submission are invisible to them. Adding standard HTML action and method attributes ensures forms work via simple HTTP requests, making them accessible to all AI agents.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Extracted forms and action/method strings across pages. Grade C; informative tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No forms NA; all attributes pass, some action coverage warns, no actions fail.
review.proposedWork: HTML-form feature for non-JS consumers. Empty/default action and method can be valid HTML; attributes alone do not prove successful submission. Keep informative.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Default self-target/GET, submitter overrides, JS-enhanced native form, invalid action, no forms and per-form evidence.

audits.title: Frames are titled
audits.purpose: Agents need a title to understand what each iframe contains. Untitled or duplicate-titled frames are opaque embedded contexts.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Per-page cached static accessibility results for visible nonnegative-tabindex frames and repeated frame titles; rules `frame-title, frame-title-unique`. Grade C; informative tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Shared A11yBackedAudit: any failure fails; incomplete without any pass warns; any pass passes; no observed applicable result NA. First failing URL and up to five selectors follow page order.
review.proposedWork: Retain element-feature or common-document scope. Missing engine output is unknown, not proven inapplicability; one pass currently masks another incomplete result. The runner strips stylesheets and does not execute JS. Preserve these coverage limits and stabilize URL/selector evidence.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Unique/missing title, hidden frame, negative tabindex and duplicate-title incomplete beside a pass. Also test all page labels, mixed pass/incomplete/missing results and permutations through the shared runner.

audits.title: Ghost-clickable elements: click targets an agent cannot address
audits.purpose: Measures the share of on-page click targets that a DOM/accessibility-tree agent cannot address at all: elements that look and behave clickable to a human or a vision model but expose no native or ARIA role and no accessible name, so they never appear in a Playwright-MCP style snapshot. Reported as semantic / (semantic + ghost) over the served markup and its same-origin stylesheets, with the reason each ghost is unaddressable.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Static native/semantic and inferred click targets, with CSS input. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No targets NA; no ghosts pass; ratio below threshold fails; other ghosts warn.
review.proposedWork: Click-target feature with declared CSS/runtime coverage. Pointer appearance is not proof of an actionable target; lack of a static signal is not proof no runtime target exists. Dossier ghost ratio and output semantic ratio need clear labels.
review.acceptanceCriteria: CSS pointer decoration, delegated handler, native unnamed target, cross-origin stylesheet, threshold and per-page counts.

audits.title: Hover-only navigation and content
audits.purpose: Detects navigation subtrees and information that exist in the DOM only while a pointer hovers — `:hover`-revealed submenus with no focus or `aria-expanded` equivalent, and content carried solely in `title` attributes or hover cards. Reports each destination URL an agent never discovers.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Hover CSS, title-only strings and hover-card heuristics across pages. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No signal and no omitted stylesheet NA. Missing paths fail/warn; no observed finding otherwise passes, including omitted CSS.
review.proposedWork: Hover feature. Unread CSS must not become a claim that every submenu has an alternative. Static ARIA markers do not prove a working focus/click route. Keep title information separate from blocked navigation.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Cross-origin-only CSS, focus-within path, inert ARIA trigger, title supplement versus unique text and hidden menu.

audits.title: Invisible Instruction Payload Scan
audits.purpose: Detect text that is present in the byte stream or DOM but not perceivable by a human, and that reads like an instruction addressed to an AI. Covers CSS-hidden text (color ≈ background, font-size:0, opacity:0, off-screen absolute positioning, zero-size + overflow:hidden, visibility:hidden, display:none), plus channels that never render at all: HTML comments, <noscript>, <template>, oversized data-* attribute values, <script type="text/plain">/application/json blobs, non-standard <meta name> content, and inline <svg><text> with fill-opacity:0 or display:none.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Text and nonrendering channels with local/same-origin CSS analysis. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No body text NA; hidden instruction patterns fail; unexplained long hidden text warns; otherwise passes.
review.proposedWork: Common scanned-channel heuristic. Report incomplete CSS and runtime limits; a pattern hit is not proof of malicious intent or successful injection. Check feature detection does not drop comment/attribute-only payloads.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Instruction quoted as documentation, template/comment-only payload, cross-origin CSS, language limits and affected channel URL.

audits.title: Form inputs have associated labels
audits.purpose: AI agents filling forms identify fields by their accessible name (label, aria-label, or aria-labelledby). Unlabeled inputs are invisible to form-filling agents, so automated workflows like "sign me up" or "submit a contact request" fail.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Per-page cached static accessibility results for native input/select names; rules `label, select-name`. Grade A; scored tier.

audits.title: Landmarks are uniquely identifiable
audits.purpose: AI browser agents traverse the accessibility tree and use a landmark’s role plus accessible name to target the right region. Two landmarks of the same role (e.g. a primary <nav> and a footer <nav>) without unique labels are indistinguishable, causing agents to act on the wrong region. A single unlabeled landmark is unambiguous and is not flagged.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Per-page cached static accessibility results for same-role landmark names; rules `landmark-unique`. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Shared A11yBackedAudit: any failure fails; incomplete without any pass warns; any pass passes; no observed applicable result NA. First failing URL and up to five selectors follow page order.
review.proposedWork: Retain element-feature or common-document scope. Missing engine output is unknown, not proven inapplicability; one pass currently masks another incomplete result. The runner strips stylesheets and does not execute JS. Preserve these coverage limits and stabilize URL/selector evidence.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Lone landmark, distinct same-role names, unnamed duplicates and hidden regions. Also test all page labels, mixed pass/incomplete/missing results and permutations through the shared runner.

audits.title: No time-based auto-refresh/redirect
audits.purpose: A <meta http-equiv="refresh"> that reloads/redirects after a delay disrupts an agent mid-read and can trap it in unexpected navigation.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Per-page cached static accessibility results for adopted refresh meta directives; rules `meta-refresh`. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Shared A11yBackedAudit: any failure fails; incomplete without any pass warns; any pass passes; no observed applicable result NA. First failing URL and up to five selectors follow page order.
review.proposedWork: Retain element-feature or common-document scope. Missing engine output is unknown, not proven inapplicability; one pass currently masks another incomplete result. The runner strips stylesheets and does not execute JS. Preserve these coverage limits and stabilize URL/selector evidence.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Absent refresh, immediate/delayed refresh, malformed delay and header-delivered refresh coverage limit. Also test all page labels, mixed pass/incomplete/missing results and permutations through the shared runner.

audits.title: Native Control Substitution Index
audits.purpose: Counts choice, date, and file-input controls implemented as custom div widgets instead of the native HTML elements, weighted by whether they sit on a conversion-critical path (search, filter, checkout, signup). Reports each substituted control with the number of agent actions it costs versus its native equivalent.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Native/custom choice, date and upload controls across pages. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No controls NA; native-only pass; broken custom contract fails; complete custom widgets warn.
review.proposedWork: Control feature. Distinguish a proven broken contract from extra interaction cost. Native equivalence and task-critical status require their own evidence; static markup cannot count actual interaction steps.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Complete APG custom widget, native wrapper, disabled/hidden widgets, no matching controls and critical versus decorative contexts.

audits.title: No nested interactive controls
audits.purpose: Interactive elements nested inside other interactive elements (e.g. a button inside a link) create ambiguous targets in the accessibility tree.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Per-page cached static accessibility results for presentational-child roles with focusable descendants; rules `nested-interactive`. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Shared A11yBackedAudit: any failure fails; incomplete without any pass warns; any pass passes; no observed applicable result NA. First failing URL and up to five selectors follow page order.
review.proposedWork: Retain element-feature or common-document scope. Missing engine output is unknown, not proven inapplicability; one pass currently masks another incomplete result. The runner strips stylesheets and does not execute JS. Preserve these coverage limits and stabilize URL/selector evidence.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Nested focusable child, nonfocusable child, native/ARIA role and hidden descendant. Also test all page labels, mixed pass/incomplete/missing results and permutations through the shared runner.

audits.title: Forms don't use blocking CAPTCHA
audits.purpose: Blocking CAPTCHAs like reCAPTCHA and hCaptcha prevent AI agents from completing forms on behalf of users. When someone asks an AI assistant to "fill out the contact form on Example.com," the CAPTCHA blocks the action entirely. Use honeypot fields or invisible server-side validation instead.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Global WAF observation and CAPTCHA selectors across selected pages. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Blocking WAF fails; no pages/unread clean sample NA; selectors warn; no selectors pass.
review.proposedWork: Common access plus adopted form feature, with per-page attribution. A widget/script is not proof it blocks a task, and scanner blocking is not proof about every agent.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Mixed wall/readable pages, nonblocking widget, missing readable evidence, rate limits and stable URL.

audits.title: The organization identifier resolves in the authoritative registry
audits.purpose: Reads `leiCode` / `iso6523Code` off the Organization markup, checks the identifier’s shape and ISO/IEC 7064 check digits locally, then resolves it against GLEIF’s public registry: exactly one record, an active entity, an issued registration, and a registered legal name that agrees with the name in the markup.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Organization identifier claims and GLEIF resolution for deduplicated LEIs. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No claims NA; invalid/mismatching LEIs fail; registry problems/advice warn; otherwise passes, potentially with zero resolved LEIs.
review.proposedWork: Declared identifier feature, not mandatory merchant identification. Deduplicate fetches without discarding distinct entity/name assertions. Malformed registry JSON is unread evidence, not proof of no record.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Same LEI claimed under two names, DUNS-only data, multiple organizations, malformed registry reply, outage and local identifier formats.

audits.title: No presentation-role conflicts
audits.purpose: An element marked role="presentation"/"none" while still focusable or carrying ARIA sends contradictory signals about whether it exists in the accessibility tree.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Per-page cached static accessibility results for presentation/none roles and empty-alt images; rules `presentation-role-conflict`. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Shared A11yBackedAudit: any failure fails; incomplete without any pass warns; any pass passes; no observed applicable result NA. First failing URL and up to five selectors follow page order.
review.proposedWork: Retain element-feature or common-document scope. Missing engine output is unknown, not proven inapplicability; one pass currently masks another incomplete result. The runner strips stylesheets and does not execute JS. Preserve these coverage limits and stabilize URL/selector evidence.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Focusable presentation, global ARIA conflict, legitimate decorative image and implicit-role filter. Also test all page labels, mixed pass/incomplete/missing results and permutations through the shared runner.

audits.title: Reflected-Parameter Injection Canary
audits.purpose: Sends at most five read-only GET probes carrying a random per-scan token, then reports whether the site echoes that token back into its title, meta description, canonical link, JSON-LD, or rendered text — the fields an answer engine lifts verbatim, which would let any third party mint a URL on this domain that shows a visiting agent arbitrary text.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: First-page readability gate, then origin query/search/path canary GET probes. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No readable entry/no probe response NA; high-trust or indexable body reflection fails; noindex body reflection warns; no echo passes.
review.proposedWork: Origin reflection experiment, not arbitrary page-purpose requirement. Escaped search text is not equivalent to executable injection. Preserve per-response escaping/sink association and partial probe coverage.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Legitimate escaped query, raw versus escaped mixed sinks, unavailable probes, mounted app, error-page reflection and first-page reorder.

audits.title: security.txt (RFC 9116)
audits.purpose: Reports whether a published /.well-known/security.txt conforms to RFC 9116 — plain text, a Contact field, and an Expires date in the future. RFC 9116 is an Informational document whose stated consumers are human security researchers and vulnerability-notification tooling; no AI crawler, retrieval pipeline or answer engine is documented to read it, so this audit is informative only — it carries weight 0 and never affects your score. A site that publishes no security.txt is reported as not applicable rather than warned.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Optional security.txt at well-known or legacy root path. Grade C; informative tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Never fetched/absent NA; HTML or malformed/expired fields warn; Contact and future Expires pass.
review.proposedWork: Retain optional artifact advisory. Name the limited field validation instead of complete RFC conformance. Page labels do not change origin-file applicability.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Absent/unread file, legacy fallback, HTML catch-all, malformed Contact URI, invalid expiry and deterministic clock.

audits.title: Stateful controls: current state readable by an agent
audits.purpose: Checks that every control whose purpose is to hold a state — toggles, switches, checkboxes, radio groups, tabs, accordions, disclosure triggers, sort direction, filter chips — exposes that state through a machine-readable attribute rather than a CSS class alone. Reports the count of state-bearing controls whose current value an agent cannot read, each with the class that carries the state instead.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: State-bearing controls inferred from markup/classes with CSS input. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No controls NA; all introspectable pass; low ratio fails; remaining opaque controls warn.
review.proposedWork: State-control feature. Static state presence does not prove updates after interaction. Keep class-name heuristics and missing stylesheet limits explicit; preserve per-page evidence.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Native state, valid ARIA state, stale state only observable at runtime, false state-class hit, partial CSS and order.

audits.title: AI-generated-image disclosure is machine-readable and self-consistent
audits.purpose: Reads `Iptc4xmpExt:DigitalSourceType` out of each image’s XMP packet and tests it against the ratified IPTC NewsCodes vocabulary. The property is typed as a URI, so a bare token, an `https` variant of the `http` vocabulary URI, a trailing slash or free text all read as nothing to a consumer. Also compares the XMP declaration against what the asset’s own C2PA manifest says.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Sampled image XMP source-type declarations with manifest substring comparison. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No adopted declarations NA; malformed/conflicting values fail; otherwise passes. Valid count subtracts findings, allowing multiple findings per asset to overcount.
review.proposedWork: Adopted disclosure feature. Name sampled assets; unread files do not establish site-wide absence. Verify same-asset assertion semantics before calling multiple historical provenance strings a contradiction.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Multiple findings on one asset, mixed capture/edit history, unread media, valid vocab URI and sample-order stability.

audits.title: No positive tabindex (logical focus order)
audits.purpose: Positive tabindex values force a non-DOM focus order. Agents that traverse the page by focus order then encounter a confusing, non-linear sequence.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Per-page cached static accessibility results for adopted tabindex values; rules `tabindex`. Grade C; informative tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Shared A11yBackedAudit: any failure fails; incomplete without any pass warns; any pass passes; no observed applicable result NA. First failing URL and up to five selectors follow page order.
review.proposedWork: Retain element-feature or common-document scope. Missing engine output is unknown, not proven inapplicability; one pass currently masks another incomplete result. The runner strips stylesheets and does not execute JS. Preserve these coverage limits and stabilize URL/selector evidence.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Absent/zero/negative/positive values, hidden element and natural DOM focus order. Also test all page labels, mixed pass/incomplete/missing results and permutations through the shared runner.

audits.title: Data tables have header associations
audits.purpose: Agents extracting tabular data rely on header↔cell associations (th scope / headers attr) to know what each value means. Missing associations make tables ambiguous.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Per-page cached static accessibility results for data tables and header associations; rules `td-has-header, th-has-data-cells, td-headers-attr, scope-attr-valid`. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Shared A11yBackedAudit: any failure fails; incomplete without any pass warns; any pass passes; no observed applicable result NA. First failing URL and up to five selectors follow page order.
review.proposedWork: Retain element-feature or common-document scope. Missing engine output is unknown, not proven inapplicability; one pass currently masks another incomplete result. The runner strips stylesheets and does not execute JS. Preserve these coverage limits and stabilize URL/selector evidence.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Small versus large table, layout table, row/column spans, explicit headers and malformed scope. Also test all page labels, mixed pass/incomplete/missing results and permutations through the shared runner.

audits.title: Third-party DOM-write blast radius
audits.purpose: Counts how many separate companies can write text into the DOM an agent reads: every registrable domain shipping a script or stylesheet into the page, judged against whether the Content-Security-Policy actually constrains what may run, and whether each resource is pinned with an `integrity` hash. Cross-origin frames with no `sandbox` are reported alongside. The origin list is the deliverable.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Pooled third-party script/style domains, integrity flags, page CSP and unsandboxed frames. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No pages/unread clean sample NA. Any weak page policy plus any unpinned domain fails; otherwise pass/warn by combined policy/frame state.
review.proposedWork: Third-party feature per resource and page. Current pooling can combine CSP absence on a script-free page with an unpinned script protected elsewhere. Keep CSS, script, frame and runtime capability claims distinct.
review.acceptanceCriteria: CSP-free page with no third parties beside protected external script, mixed integrity, script-src none, multiple policies and runtime injection limits.

audits.title: trust.txt associations are reciprocated and agree with robots.txt
audits.purpose: For publishers who maintain a trust.txt: validates the attribute names, resolves each `belongto=` against that association’s own trust.txt to see whether it lists this domain back, and compares `datatrainingallowed=` against what robots.txt actually tells AI crawlers. Reported as a trust signal only — no AI engine is documented as a trust.txt consumer, so nothing here affects the score.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Optional origin trust.txt, bounded reciprocal-domain probes and root robots policy. Grade C; informative tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Absent artifact NA; observations warn; no observations passes.
review.proposedWork: Optional unscored declaration feature. Crawl allowance is not permission to train. HTML catch-all/empty parsed entries cannot prove a valid trust file. Retain incomplete association coverage.
review.acceptanceCriteria: No file, HTML catch-all, empty parse, failed reciprocal fetch, intentional training deny with crawl allow and capped associations.

audits.title: UGC Trust-Boundary Markers
audits.purpose: Locates visitor-contributed regions — comments, reviews, Q&A, forum posts, submission forms — and checks whether any machine-readable boundary separates them from editorial copy: `data-nosnippet` containment on a span, div or section, `rel="ugc"` on their outbound links, and whether raw markup survives the sanitizer inside them.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Visitor-content region heuristics, markup and instruction patterns across pages. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No regions NA; dangerous/payload findings fail; unbounded regions warn; bounded/marked pass.
review.proposedWork: UGC feature with explicit provenance evidence. rel=ugc/data-nosnippet are consumer-specific signals, not sanitizer or prompt-injection guarantees. Do not force useful forum answers out of all snippets.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Editorial content resembling comments, valid user images, marked link beside unbounded text, sanitizer survivors and instruction quotations.

audits.title: Invisible codepoints carrying hidden text
audits.purpose: Scans rendered text, the attributes an agent reads, every JSON-LD string value and the site’s root files for codepoints that carry information invisibly: the Unicode Tags block (U+E0000–U+E007F), bidirectional overrides and isolates (U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069), and zero-width or filler characters (U+200B–U+200D, U+2060, U+FEFF, U+00AD, U+115F, U+1160, U+3164, U+FFA0). Decodes any tag-block run back to ASCII and prints the invisible sentence sitting on the page.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Page text/attributes and selected root files scanned for codepoint patterns. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No input/unread clean text NA; tag/bidi/high zero-width matches fail; lower-count matches warn; no hits pass.
review.proposedWork: Common scanned-text heuristic, with channel-specific attribution. Legitimate script shaping, emoji sequences and quotations need exclusions. Aggregate thresholds must not manufacture a per-page density defect.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Indic joiners, emoji tags, bidirectional language, legal soft hyphens, repeated low-density pages and root-only evidence.

audits.title: State-changing links an agent can trigger by fetching them
audits.purpose: Finds links and GET forms whose URL changes state on the server — delete, cancel, revoke, unsubscribe, logout, add-to-cart, confirm — with no POST, no confirmation affordance and no `rel="nofollow"` in the way. Markup analysis only: a flagged URL is reported, never fetched.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: URL/label patterns on links and GET forms; confirmation/nofollow/robots hints. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No pages/unread clean sample NA; suspect links fail, forms warn, none passes.
review.proposedWork: Observed possible action feature. A URL pattern cannot prove a server mutation or absence of server-side confirmation. Never trigger destructive endpoints to strengthen this check; retain static uncertainty.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Delete documentation URL, confirmation route, real action-shaped GET, POST alternative, nofollow limits and stable URL evidence.

audits.title: Listings walkable by URL: pagination and facet fallback
audits.purpose: Checks that a listing exposes its later pages through real `href` pagination or a `rel="next"` link rather than infinite-scroll machinery alone, and that each facet changes what the server returns rather than only what the browser shows. Reports the deepest item index reachable by URL alone, and any facet that turns out to be client-only.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `category`, plus internal `pagesOfType`; local `surveyListing` reads pagination links and probes at most two facet URLs per page through `fetchSampledPage`. Grade B.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: no category NA; truncated listing/sentinel failure takes precedence; button/client-facet limits warn; otherwise passes.
review.proposedWork: listing/filter/pagination feature in the documented population. A non-commerce listing can need the same navigation, but do not claim every tab/state is covered. The current deepest index multiplies item count by a URL number; it does not walk pagination. Equal item counts after a filter do not prove client-only filtering. Report observed versus inferred reachability and unread probes; expose facet sampling limits.
review.acceptanceCriteria: non-commerce listing, no pagination, real next link, client-only control, offset versus page number, same-count different filtered items, fetch failure, more than two facets and stable worst-page evidence.

audits.title: The Wikidata entity this site claims points back at this site
audits.purpose: Takes the Wikidata Q-id the site claims in its Organization or Person `sameAs`, asks Wikidata what that entity gives as its official website (P856), and compares registrable domains. A `sameAs` is self-asserted and any site can claim any entity; only the round trip is evidence.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Declared Wikidata entities and bounded official-website lookups. Grade B; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No claims NA; mismatching domain fails; absent/unread/alternate-domain evidence warns; otherwise passes.
review.proposedWork: Declared entity feature. A related person/publisher can have a different official site; distinguish owner identity from referenced entity. Multiple official websites and sample limits must remain visible.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Related person entity, multi-domain organization, multiple P856 values, registry outage, no claim and stable capped entity order.

audits.title: Advanced product details
audits.purpose: AI agents use a product's name, brand, category, and availability status to filter search results and answer availability queries. A Product without a name cannot be matched to a catalog entry at all; missing brand, category or availability makes it less likely to surface in filtered AI recommendations.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `product`; flattened product nodes, first product and its offers. Grade A.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: no product node fails; first node's name, brand/manufacturer, category and availability decide pass/warn/fail.
review.proposedWork: confirmed product purpose for presence; present primary product for content validation. Do not allow a related product to satisfy the page or report only the first product in a multi-page sample.
review.acceptanceCriteria: product without schema, related-product cards, absent versus broken product data, two unequal PDPs and node/page permutations.

audits.title: Article schema
audits.purpose: AI agents extract Article schema to identify content freshness (datePublished/dateModified), authorship, and topic (headline). Without it, your blog content is treated as generic text with no provenance, reducing its chances of being cited in AI-generated answers.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `content`; `isArticlePage` returns true for every selected page. First Article/NewsArticle/BlogPosting per page. Grade A.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: all complete passes, any present warns, none fails; empty sample NA. Required fields include `dateModified`.
review.proposedWork: positive article purpose with independent evidence. Validate the primary article and recheck required versus recommended fields against the dossier before making an unchanged article invent an update date.
review.acceptanceCriteria: privacy/contact pages, article missing schema, related article cards, multiple article nodes, unchanged article, partial and malformed markup.

audits.title: Author schema with credentials
audits.purpose: AI systems assign higher confidence to content from named experts with verifiable credentials. Person schema with jobTitle, sameAs, and affiliation lets AI agents cross-reference author identity across platforms, boosting your content in RAG trust scoring.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `content`; Person nodes and article author objects across the sample. Grade C, informative.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: none fails; any person with name, jobTitle, sameAs and affiliation passes; otherwise warns.
review.proposedWork: authorship feature or supported article purpose. Bind a person to the assessed article. Optional enrichment absence must not become a requirement for every page; retain unscored advice.
review.acceptanceCriteria: unrelated employee Person, organizational author, linked author references, absent authorship, incomplete optional fields and mixed articles.

audits.title: BreadcrumbList schema
audits.purpose: AI agents use BreadcrumbList to understand your site hierarchy and navigate between parent/child pages. Without breadcrumbs, agents cannot infer where a page sits in your content tree, making it harder to provide contextual answers that reference related pages.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current category/product/content; URL path depth over one segment selects pages, then BreadcrumbList presence. Grade A.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: all covered passes, some warns, none fails; no deep URL warns. URL depth supplies the hierarchy assumption.
review.proposedWork: establish navigational hierarchy independently. Locale or deployment path depth alone cannot require breadcrumbs. No eligible hierarchy NA.
review.acceptanceCriteria: locale prefixes, mounted apps, shallow hierarchical pages, deep standalone pages, missing breadcrumb schema and partial coverage.

audits.title: ClaimReview investment advisory
audits.purpose: ADVISORY / UNSCORED. Detects ClaimReview markup and tells the operator the truth about its status rather than rewarding coverage: Google is phasing out ClaimReview support in Search, while the Fact Check Explorer still consumes it. Also validates the required shape and the one-per-page constraint for sites that keep it.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: ClaimReview nodes and counts per selected page. Grade A; informative tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No adopted markup NA. Missing fields, rating labels or multiple nodes warn; otherwise passes.
review.proposedWork: Retain advisory artifact scope. Separate currently supported consumer shape from historical Search eligibility. Stabilize node/URL examples and associate defects with their own page.
review.acceptanceCriteria: No adoption, valid and defective nodes on different pages, multiple reviews, rating formats and stable affected URL.

audits.title: FAQPage schema
audits.purpose: AI answer engines like Perplexity and Google SGE extract FAQ-structured content with higher confidence for direct answers. FAQPage schema makes your Q&A content machine-readable, giving it priority in AI-generated responses over unstructured text.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Pages selected by question-shaped headings; FAQPage presence. Grade C; informative tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No matching pages warns; all FAQ-covered pass, some warn, none fail.
review.proposedWork: Keep informative. Question headings do not establish the specialist FAQ rich-result population. No eligible FAQ feature should be NA; avoid unsupported answer-priority claims.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Non-FAQ question heading, genuine FAQ without markup, no questions, malformed FAQ markup and mixed pages.

audits.title: HowTo schema
audits.purpose: AI agents use HowTo schema to present step-by-step instructions as structured answers. Without it, agents must parse your numbered headings heuristically, which often breaks step ordering or misses steps entirely.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `content`; numbered sequential headings imply instructions; checks HowTo step arrays. Grade C, informative.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: no candidate warns; all marked passes, partial warns, none fails.
review.proposedWork: instructional feature; no candidate NA. Keep grade C and avoid implying documented adoption. Separate an ordered list from actual instructions.
review.acceptanceCriteria: numbered legal clauses, recipe/tutorial intent, non-content page with steps, absent versus malformed HowTo and partial coverage.

audits.title: JSON-LD present
audits.purpose: AI agents rely on JSON-LD structured data to understand what your site offers, who runs it, and how to interact with it. Without any JSON-LD, agents like ChatGPT and Perplexity treat your site as unstructured text with no machine-readable identity. Add Organization and WebSite schemas to your homepage <head> as a starting point.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Parsed JSON-LD blocks pooled across selected pages. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: Any block passes; no blocks or no pages fail.
review.proposedWork: Distinguish site-level detection from page-level obligations. Valid alternative encodings and pages without a supported structured-data use case must not inherit a JSON-LD requirement. Keep malformed-present separate from absent.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Empty sample, Microdata/RDFa-only page, unrelated schema on another page and eligible entity missing all markup.

audits.title: LocalBusiness/ProfessionalService schema
audits.purpose: AI agents use LocalBusiness schema to answer location-based queries like "find a [service] near me." Without it, your business is invisible to location-aware AI systems. Add address, telephone, and openingHours to help agents provide accurate local recommendations.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `homepage`; PostalAddress plus a locator link implies physical presence, then scans all selected nodes. Grade A.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: no physical signals NA; any matching LocalBusiness/ProfessionalService passes; otherwise fails.
review.proposedWork: explicit physical-business site context; postal contact alone is insufficient. Review subtype handling and primary-business identity. Avoid a guard that requires the schema being tested to establish eligibility.
review.acceptanceCriteria: online-only business with mailing address, real store without schema, business subtypes, locator elsewhere and unrelated business nodes.

audits.title: Organization schema
audits.purpose: AI agents use Organization schema to identify your brand, logo, and contact info. Without it, agents cannot confidently attribute content to your organization or display your branding in AI-generated answers. Add this JSON-LD to your homepage <head>.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `homepage`; organization nodes across selected pages, then the first node's name, URL and logo. Grade A.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: no organization fails; first complete node passes, incomplete warns. Other nodes do not repair first-node selection.
review.proposedWork: keep a site-identity claim with explicit entity ownership. Review about/contact evidence as possible inputs; do not require an organization on every page or conflate unrelated publishers. Check required versus recommended fields.
review.acceptanceCriteria: primary versus related organization, alternate identity page, multiple nodes, absent logo, no eligible identity page and node permutations.

audits.title: Review/AggregateRating schema
audits.purpose: AI agents use Review/AggregateRating schema as social proof when comparing options. When a user asks "what is the best X?", agents surface structured ratings from schema rather than parsing unstructured testimonial text. Add this schema to make your reviews machine-readable.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current homepage/product; review components, widgets, or review markup; reads structured data formats. Grade A.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: no review content NA. Aggregates usable reviews/ratings; URL patterns and Product attachment decide product coverage. Dossier deliberately accepts at least one rated product in the sample.
review.proposedWork: review feature plus supported review target. Replace hidden URL-based product guessing with shared purpose evidence. Retain the explicit sample claim until a dossier revision supports per-page requirements.
review.acceptanceCriteria: no reviews, visible reviews without schema, product versus organization ratings, custom product URLs and mixed review-target samples.

audits.title: Schema validation
audits.purpose: AI agents parse @context and @type to identify entity types in your structured data. Blocks missing these properties are silently ignored by every schema consumer, including Google, ChatGPT plugins, and RAG pipelines. Add "@context": "https://schema.org" and a valid @type to each block.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: Flattened structured-data nodes, excluding graph wrappers and reference-only nodes. Grade A; scored tier.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: No nodes fail; any retained node without context/type fails; otherwise passes.
review.proposedWork: Adopted structured-data feature; absence NA. Validate inherited context and node/reference semantics before requiring fields on each flattened object. Current pass is not full schema validation.
review.acceptanceCriteria: Absent markup, inherited graph context, reference-only objects, invalid JSON beside valid nodes and page permutations.

audits.title: Service schema
audits.purpose: AI agents use Service schema to understand what you offer and who provides it. Without it, agents must infer your offerings from unstructured text, which leads to inaccurate or incomplete descriptions in AI-generated recommendations.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current homepage/content; Service/ProfessionalService, service-like paths or services links imply intent. Grade A.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: no intent NA; intent with no nodes fails; any complete name/provider node passes; otherwise warns across the selected sample.
review.proposedWork: service-offering purpose or present service feature. A shared navigation link, especially an external link, must not make every page a service. Define whether the claim concerns site coverage or each offering before aggregation changes.
review.acceptanceCriteria: shared services navigation, external link, real offering without schema, unrelated complete node and two offerings with unequal coverage.

audits.title: Speakable schema
audits.purpose: Google Assistant uses the speakable property to pick which sentences of a news article it reads aloud on Assistant-enabled devices. Without it, the assistant has to guess, and often vocalizes navigation or boilerplate instead of your headline and summary. Mark the headline and summary with cssSelector on your Article or WebPage node.

review.baselinePopulationAndRead: current `content`; article helper accepts every page. Reads nonempty cssSelector/xpath on Article/Page/Posting hosts. Grade B.
review.baselineAggregationAndAbsence: all covered passes, some warns, none fails; empty sample NA. Does not establish the narrower consumer population.
review.proposedWork: dossier documents a limited English-news consumer, not all articles. Require that supported population or a present adopted feature. Preserve uncertainty and refresh the dossier's consumer-retirement trigger before enabling broader scoring. Do not infer live support from this review.
review.acceptanceCriteria: general content, non-news article, non-English news, uncertain publisher eligibility, valid selector forms, missing targets and partial coverage.
